dataset_scope: Spring 2026 curated snapshot for CSS 382 MVP
notes: This seed dataset is a manually curated academic snapshot for HuskyAdvisor. It is intentionally small, transparent, and designed for course recommendation demos rather than official advising use.

courses.title: Foundations of Computing
courses.prerequisites: Admission to upper-division CSS coursework or department guidance.
courses.description: Survey of core ideas in computing: data representation, algorithms, abstraction, and software engineering practice. Prepares students for upper-division CSS coursework with collaborative projects and introductory programming exercises.

courses.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
courses.description: Design and analysis of fundamental data structures including lists, trees, heaps, hash tables, and graphs. Algorithmic techniques such as sorting, searching, recursion, and graph traversal. Emphasis on complexity analysis and implementation trade-offs.

courses.title: Software Engineering
courses.description: Principles of software development life cycle, requirements engineering, design modeling, testing strategies, version control, and team collaboration. Students apply agile methods to build a multi-component software system.

courses.title: Database Systems
courses.description: Relational modeling, SQL, schema design, normalization, and transaction concepts for data-intensive applications.

courses.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Introduces foundational AI topics such as search, reasoning, and intelligent behavior in software systems.

courses.title: Information Assurance and Cybersecurity
courses.prerequisites: Programming background and upper-division readiness recommended.
courses.description: Introduces core cybersecurity and information assurance concepts for protecting computing systems and digital infrastructure.

courses.title: Secure Systems
courses.description: Covers system security principles, secure design, and common ways computing systems can fail or be attacked.

courses.title: Hardware and Computer Organization
courses.description: Explores lower-level machine organization, performance tradeoffs, and system interfaces relevant to hardware-software collaboration.

courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.description: Processes and threads, CPU scheduling, synchronization and deadlocks, memory management, virtual memory, file systems, and I/O subsystems. Hands-on labs reinforce concepts using a contemporary operating system.

courses.title: Networking and Distributed Systems
courses.description: Networking fundamentals and distributed-system design for mission-critical and connected software systems.

courses.title: Cloud Computing
courses.description: Distributed services, cloud deployment, and scalable architectures useful for enterprise software environments.

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence
courses.prerequisites: CSS 342 and discrete math background recommended.
courses.description: Introduces search, knowledge representation, reasoning, and core AI methods for intelligent software systems.

courses.title: Embedded Systems
courses.description: Explores embedded computing and hardware-software interaction in constrained real-world systems.

courses.title: Security and Privacy
courses.description: Core security principles, common vulnerabilities, secure design thinking, and privacy concerns in modern computing environments.

courses.title: Software Testing and Quality Assurance
courses.description: Verification, validation, and dependable software development practices for production-grade systems.

courses.title: Database Systems
courses.prerequisites: CSS 370 or comparable database preparation recommended.
courses.description: Advanced database systems course for students interested in backend, data-intensive, and enterprise software applications.

courses.title: Web Programming and Applications
courses.description: Builds practical experience with modern web application development and interactive software systems.

courses.title: Machine Intelligence
courses.prerequisites: Algorithmic preparation and mathematical maturity recommended.
courses.description: AI-oriented elective that supports machine intelligence and data-driven software pathways.

courses.title: Business Data Analysis
courses.description: Applies quantitative reasoning and data interpretation to practical decision-making in organizational settings.

courses.title: Information Systems Analysis
courses.description: Covers information systems planning, stakeholder needs, and structured approaches to analyzing organizational technology problems.

courses.title: Business Systems Applications
courses.description: Applies computing tools to practical business systems and organizational problem solving.

courses.title: Business Intelligence
courses.description: Focuses on reporting, dashboards, and turning data into actionable information for organizational decision-making.

courses.title: Digital Circuits and Systems
courses.prerequisites: Calculus and introductory physics or department guidance.
courses.description: Introduces combinational and sequential logic, digital design, and system-level thinking for electronics.

courses.title: Signals and Systems
courses.description: Models continuous and discrete signals, system response, and analysis tools used across electrical and embedded engineering contexts.

courses.title: Electronics
courses.prerequisites: Engineering math and circuit fundamentals recommended.
courses.description: Focuses on electronic components and circuit behavior used in practical device and embedded-system contexts.

courses.title: Embedded Systems Design
courses.description: Microcontrollers, hardware-software integration, and real-world system constraints common in embedded engineering.

courses.title: Control Systems
courses.description: Studies feedback, stability, and control concepts used in engineering systems and device-level automation.

courses.title: Business Communication
courses.description: Professional writing and presentation skills for business contexts, including collaboration and reporting.

courses.title: Matrix Algebra with Applications
courses.prerequisites: Precalculus and introductory college math sequence.
courses.description: Linear systems, matrices, eigenvalues, and applications in computing, graphics, and machine learning.
